content.title: Real-Number Properties and Number-Line Relationships
content.overview: This lesson focuses on visualizing and calculating positions on a one-dimensional number line. You will learn to identify coordinates, calculate midpoints between two points, and determine new positions based on specific distances and directions.
learning_objectives: Calculate the midpoint between two coordinates on a number line.
Determine the distance between any two points using absolute value.
Apply directional movement (left or right) to find new coordinates from a reference point.

sections.title: The Number Line and Distance
sections.content: A number line represents real numbers as points in space. The distance between any two points, x and y, is calculated using the absolute value of their difference: |x - y|. Because distance is a measure of magnitude, it is always non-negative. When moving along the number line, direction is indicated by the sign of the operation: adding a value moves you to the right (positive direction), while subtracting a value moves you to the left (negative direction).

sections.title: Finding the Midpoint
sections.content: The midpoint is the exact center between two points on a number line. To find the midpoint of two coordinates, x1 and x2, you calculate their arithmetic mean (average). The formula is: Midpoint = (x1 + x2) / 2. This resulting value is equidistant from both endpoints.

sections.title: The Midpoint-and-Step Strategy
sections.content:
ACT problems often require finding a point based on its relationship to a midpoint. The Midpoint-and-Step strategy involves three steps: 1. Identify and label the given endpoint coordinates. 2. Calculate the midpoint using the average formula. 3. Apply the required movement by adding the distance if moving right, or subtracting the distance if moving left.

![A number line showing points P at -2, Q at 3, and their midpoint R at 0.5, with an arrow moving 4 units right to point S at 4.5.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/a923307d-8682-4e7e-8d22-fea0be1d6faa-1786505457812-922.webp)

worked_examples.question: On a number line, point A is at -5 and point B is at 7. Point M is the midpoint of segment AB. Point K is located 6 units to the left of point M. What is the coordinate of point K?
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Identify endpoints A = -5 and B = 7. Step 2: Calculate the midpoint M. M = (-5 + 7) / 2 = 2 / 2 = 1. Step 3: Determine the movement for point K. Since K is 6 units to the left of M, subtract 6 from the coordinate of M. K = 1 - 6 = -5. Verification: The distance |K - M| is |-5 - 1| = 6, which matches the problem statement.

common_mistakes: Subtracting coordinates to find the midpoint instead of averaging them.
Confusing direction: adding when the problem specifies moving to the left.
Applying the distance to one of the endpoints instead of the midpoint as requested.
Forgetting that the average of a negative and positive number requires keeping the negative sign (e.g., thinking -2 + 4 is 6 instead of 2).
exam_tips: Always draw a quick sketch of the number line to visualize the relative positions of points.
Check your midpoint by ensuring the distance to each endpoint is identical.
Read carefully to see if the distance is applied to an endpoint or the midpoint.
content.recap: To solve number line problems, average the endpoints to find the midpoint and then add or subtract the specified distance based on the direction (right or left) to find the final coordinate.

knowledge_claims.content: The midpoint of two coordinates x1 and x2 on a number line is calculated as (x1 + x2) / 2.
The distance between two points x and y on a number line is given by the absolute value expression |x - y|.
Moving to the right on a number line requires adding the distance to the starting coordinate.
Moving to the left on a number line requires subtracting the distance from the starting coordinate.
A midpoint is the point on a line segment that is equidistant from both endpoints.
To find a point S that is a distance 'd' to the right of a midpoint R, first calculate R = (x1 + x2) / 2, then calculate S = R + d.
A common error is calculating the difference (x2 - x1) instead of the average (x1 + x2) / 2 when looking for a midpoint.
To verify a calculated coordinate S is a distance 'd' from point R, check if |S - R| equals 'd'.
On a number line, a negative coordinate indicates a position to the left of zero, while a positive coordinate indicates a position to the right of zero.
If point P is at -2 and point Q is at 3, their midpoint R is 0.5.
The phrase 'to the right of' in a number line problem serves as a trigger to use addition.
The phrase 'to the left of' in a number line problem serves as a trigger to use subtraction.
